questions.prompt: Using the model for Vanishing Heat Capacity and Thermal Expansion, set up the governing equation, inequality, derivative, probability, or phase-rule count and solve the following problem: A solid has \(C_{\mathrm{tot},p}=aT^3\) below \(5\,\mathrm K\), with \(a=2.0\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-4}}\). Find \(C_{\mathrm{tot},p}\) and \(S(T)-S_0\) at \(T=2.0\,\mathrm K\).
questions.answer:
Model:
Apply the model for Vanishing Heat Capacity and Thermal Expansion under every condition stated in the question; use SI units unless another unit is explicitly supplied.

Working:
The heat capacity is \[C_{\mathrm{tot},p}=aT^3=(2.0\times10^{-3})(2.0)^3\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}=1.6\times10^{-2}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}.\] Apply equation \([2]\): \[S(T)-S_0=\int_0^T aT'^2\,dT'=\frac{aT^3}{3}=5.3\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}.\] Both expressions vanish with positive powers of temperature. Final result: at \(2.0\,\mathrm K\), \(C_{\mathrm{tot},p}=1.6\times10^{-2}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}\) and \(S-S_0=5.3\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}\).

Final answer:
At \(2.0\,\mathrm K\), \(C_{\mathrm{tot},p}=1.6\times10^{-2}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}\) and \(S-S_0=5.3\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}\).

Check:
Substituting the result back into the defining relation reproduces the stated data to the quoted precision. The final unit follows from the equation, and the qualitative trend agrees with the model.

questions.answer:
